recipes.title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of Swedish meatballs with cream gravy, mashed potato, lingonberries, and pickled cucumber
recipes.prep_alt: Meatballs frying and browning in a hot pan

sections.heading: Steps
items: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk in a small bowl for 5 minutes, until softened into a paste.

In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, ground pork, soaked breadcrumbs, egg, grated onion, allspice, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix gently with your hands just until combined — overmixing makes tough meatballs.
Roll into small, walnut-sized meatballs (about 1 inch/2.5cm), keeping them uniform so they cook evenly.

Ask an adult to help melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry the meatballs in batches, turning often, 8–10 minutes, until deeply browned all over and cooked through with no pink in the middle. Transfer to a plate.
In the same skillet, melt the gravy butter and whisk in the flour, cooking 1 minute to remove the raw taste.

Gradually whisk in the beef broth and cream, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer 3–5 minutes, stirring, until thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon. Stir in the soy sauce.
Return the meatballs to the gravy and simmer 2–3 minutes to warm through and coat.
Serve hot over mashed potatoes with a spoonful of lingonberry jam alongside.

recipes.title: Baked Norwegian Salmon with Dill Sauce
recipes.dish_alt: A baked salmon fillet topped with a creamy dill sauce, served on a plate
recipes.prep_alt: A raw salmon fillet drizzled with olive oil and scattered with fresh herbs, ready to bake

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Place the salmon fillet skin-side down in a lightly oiled baking dish. Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice, then season with salt and pepper.
Bake 12–15 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and is just opaque in the center.
While the salmon bakes, whisk together the sour cream, chopped dill, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and garlic (if using) in a small bowl.
Let the salmon rest 2 minutes, then serve topped with a generous spoonful of the dill sauce, alongside boiled potatoes.

recipes.title: Swedish Yellow Pea Soup (Ärtsoppa)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of thick, golden Swedish yellow pea soup served with rye crispbread and pickled cucumber
recipes.prep_alt: A container of dried yellow split peas, ready for overnight soaking

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Smoked pork hock, or thick-cut bacon/salt pork

sections.heading: Steps
items: The night before, place the dried yellow split peas in a large bowl, cover with plenty of cold water, and soak at least 8 hours (or overnight).
Drain and rinse the peas, then add them to a large pot with the water or stock. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam that rises to the top.
Add the pork hock (or bacon) and diced onion. Reduce the heat to low, cover partially, and simmer 1 to 1½ hours, stirring occasionally, until the peas are completely soft and starting to break apart.
Ask an adult to help remove the pork from the pot, cut it into bite-sized cubes (discarding any skin or bone), and return it to the soup.
Stir in the thyme and marjoram, then season with salt and pepper. Simmer another 10 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Ladle into bowls and serve with a dollop of mustard and crispbread on the side.

recipes.title: Finnish Karelian Stew (Karjalanpaisti)
recipes.dish_alt: A clay pot of Finnish Karelian stew with tender braised beef and pork, served with boiled potatoes
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Chopping the Onion and Carrot
recipes.prep_alt: Diced onion and carrot on a wooden cutting board with a chef's knife

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F).
Layer the cubed beef and pork in a large Dutch oven or heavy oven-safe pot with the sliced onion and carrot.
Add the water or stock, whole allspice berries, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Cover tightly and place in the oven. Braise 2½ to 3 hours, until the meat is completely fall-apart tender.
Season to taste with more salt and pepper if needed.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes and a spoonful of lingonberry jam alongside.

recipes.title: Danish Meatballs (Frikadeller)
recipes.dish_alt: Oval Danish frikadeller patties with boiled potatoes, brown gravy, and a fresh salad
recipes.prep_alt: Raw oval-shaped meatball patties arranged on a cutting board, ready to fry

sections.heading: Steps
items: In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, ground beef, grated onion, egg, flour, and milk. Season with salt and pepper.
Mix well with your hands until the mixture is smooth and slightly sticky, then let it rest in the fridge for 10 minutes to firm up.
Using two spoons or wet hands, shape the mixture into oval patties about 2 inches long and ½ inch thick.

Ask an adult to help melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry the patties 4–5 minutes per side, until deeply golden brown and cooked through with no pink in the middle. Transfer to a plate.
In the same skillet, melt the gravy butter and whisk in the flour, cooking 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer 3–4 minutes, until thickened.
Serve the frikadeller hot with the gravy, boiled potatoes, and pickled red cabbage.

recipes.title: Norwegian Fish Cakes (Fiskekaker)
recipes.dish_alt: Golden pan-fried Norwegian fish cakes on greens with a dollop of cream sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Two raw skinless cod fillets on a white background, ready to be minced

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help finely chop or pulse the fish in a food processor until roughly minced, not fully pureed — a little texture is traditional.
In a large bowl, mix the mashed potato with the minced fish, egg, flour, milk, grated onion, salt, nutmeg, and white pepper until well combined.
Cover and refrigerate the mixture 15 minutes to firm up.
Wet your hands and shape the mixture into small, flat patties about 2½ inches wide.
Ask an adult to help melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the fish cakes 3–4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes and a dollop of sour cream-mustard sauce.

recipes.title: Swedish Cabbage Rolls (Kåldolmar)
recipes.dish_alt: Swedish cabbage rolls simmered in a pan with pan juices
recipes.prep_alt: Raw stuffed cabbage rolls arranged on a plate before cooking

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Boiled or mashed potatoes, to serve

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Core the cabbage and blanch the whole leaves 2–3 minutes, until pliable. Drain and let cool, then trim the thick center rib flat with a knife so the leaves roll easily.
In a bowl, mix the ground beef, ground pork, cooked rice, chopped onion, egg, milk, allspice, salt, and pepper until combined.
Place a spoonful of the meat mixture at the base of each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly into a neat parcel.
Ask an adult to help melt the butter in a large oven-safe pot or skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the cabbage rolls on all sides, 3–4 minutes total.
Pour in the beef broth and drizzle the syrup over the rolls. Cover and simmer gently 45–50 minutes, until the cabbage is tender and the filling is cooked through.
Serve hot with the pan juices spooned over, alongside boiled or mashed potatoes and a spoonful of lingonberry jam.

recipes.title: Swedish Cinnamon Buns (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: A cardamom-spiced Swedish cinnamon bun topped with pearl sugar on a plate
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Unbaked Buns, Ready to Rise
recipes.prep_alt: Rows of unbaked cinnamon-swirled dough buns on a tray, ready for their final rise before baking

sections.heading: Steps
items: In a small bowl, stir the lukewarm milk and yeast together and let sit 5 minutes, until foamy.

In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, cardamom, and salt. Add the yeast mixture, softened butter, and beaten egg. Mix and knead (by hand or with a dough hook) 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rise in a warm spot 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Ask an adult to help roll the dough out on a floured surface into a large rectangle, about ¼ inch thick.
Spread the softened filling butter evenly over the dough, then sprinkle with the brown sugar, cinnamon, and cardamom.
Fold the dough into thirds like a letter, then cut into long, thin strips. Twist each strip and coil it into a knot to shape the classic kanelbullar knot.
Place the buns on a lined baking sheet, cover, and let rise 30–45 minutes, until puffy.
Ask an adult to help preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Brush the buns with the egg wash and sprinkle with pearl sugar or sliced almonds.
Bake 8–10 minutes, until golden brown. Cool slightly on a wire rack before serving warm.
